title: An overload set
description:
Implement the four overloads of `countOf` documented below (lesson 1.03). Read each overload's description: they do not all count the same way.

```cpp-norun
std::size_t countOf(std::string_view text, char c);                        // (1)
std::size_t countOf(std::string_view text, std::string_view word);         // (2)
std::size_t countOf(const std::vector<int>& values, int value);            // (3)
template<class Pred>
std::size_t countOf(const std::vector<int>& values, Pred pred);            // (4)
```

1. The number of characters in `text` equal to `c`.
2. The number of **non-overlapping** occurrences of `word` in `text`, searching from the left: after a match, the search continues after the end of that match. If `word` is empty, the result is `text.size() + 1` (an empty word is found before every character and at the end).
3. The number of elements equal to `value`.
4. The number of elements `x` for which `pred(x)` returns true. `pred` is called exactly once per element, in order.

**Complexity**: (1), (3) and (4) are linear in the size of the input; (2) is at most linear in `text.size()` times `word.size()`.
hints: For (2), `std::string_view::find(word, from)` returns the position of the next match at or after `from`. To avoid overlaps, start the next search at `match + word.size()`, not `match + 1`.
Check which overload each test calls: `countOf(v, 3)` is (3) because a non-template exact match beats the template (4); `countOf("abc", "")` is (2) because a string literal cannot become a `char`.
